The mobile operator of the churn deck has tested its retention e-mail in Germany and Spain. The CRM manager asks: **did the first name work in both markets, how big must the next test be, and which e-mail should we send?**

| Step | What | Time |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Coding exercise** in pairs: Tasks 1 to 4 below with the packages (polars, statsmodels, plotnine) | 35 minutes |
| 2 | **Plenary**: the answers | 5 minutes |
| 3 | **Posit Assistant**: the same tasks with the assistant; compare its code, numbers and wording with yours (last section) | 10 minutes |

Use `ab_testing.qmd` as a template: each task names the step whose code you can reuse. Every effect is an OLS regression on 0/1 dummies: coefficient × 100 = percentage points (pp). Write Germany and Spain as two plain blocks of code; repeating two lines is fine. Deliverable: one slide per pair with the interaction plot and two sentences for the CRM manager.

## The data

Two simulated experiments with 40,000 customers each, both randomised within each country. `data/abtest/email_ab.csv` is the A/B test of the subject line: `country` (DE, ES), `device` (mobile, desktop), `version` (A = generic subject line, the control; B = with the customer's first name, the test), `split` (the same as a dummy: 0 = A, 1 = B), `clicked` (1 = clicked the link to the loyalty offers) and `unsubscribed` (1 = left the mailing list). `data/abtest/email_factorial.csv` is the 2 × 2 test of the next campaign, with the same `country`, `device`, `clicked` and `unsubscribed` columns and two dummies: `personal` (1 = first name in the subject line) and `discount` (1 = 10 % off the next bill). This file sits in `sessions/01-foundations/`, so it reads the data two folders up (`../../data/...`). Run the first cell as it is.

```{python}
import polars as pl
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
from plotnine import aes, geom_line, geom_point, ggplot, labs
from statsmodels.stats.power import NormalIndPower
from statsmodels.stats.proportion import proportion_effectsize

ab = pl.read_csv("../../data/abtest/email_ab.csv")
fa = pl.read_csv("../../data/abtest/email_factorial.csv")
```
